newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close little changed.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close little changed.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended virtually unchanged despite a strong rise in Bancoquia on the back of news that Spain's Banco Santander was to buy a stake in the bank, the country's eighth largest in terms of assets.

Bogota's IBB index drifted up 0.02 percent to 832.98 amid a higher than average 20 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED index ended fractionally lower at 13,212.81 in an 8.8 billion peso volume.

"There was heavy demand for Bancoquia after the rumors that had been floating around for several days were confirmed, but most of the volume was tied up in big cross deals in the Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate," one Bogota broker said.

Bancoquia rose 9.48 percent to 2,400 in Bogota, while in Medellin it rose 9.49 percent to 2,400. The total volume on the two exchanges in Bancoquia was 656 million pesos. The rise was sparked by confirmation that the Grupo Santander had agreed to buy a 55 percent stake, worth $151 million, in Bancoquia. The deal still has to be approved by the Colombian and Spanish authorities.

The big volumes in Bogota, however, were concentrated in cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, part of the Sindicato Antioqueno, down 0.09 percent to 5,195 in a 7.8 billion peso volume, and in the rarely-traded real estate developer Desarrolladora Inmobiliaria de Las Americas, which ended at 1.2 pesos per share in a 9.5 billion peso volume.

On the Medellin exchange volumes centered on chocolate manufacturer Nacional de Chocolates, which remained stable at 8,300 amid a 1.6 billion peso volume. Cementos Caribe fell 0.47 percent to 4,280, finance company Corfinsura edged up 0.06 percent to 1,751 and Cemento Argos dropped 0.1 percent. All are part of the Sindicato Antioqueno.
